children: U.K. retail footfall fell on year in August, but improved compared with July, as cooler weather saw consumers hit the shops for essentials and back-to-school items, according to data from the British Retail Consortium. Over the month, total U.K. footfall fell 1.7% from August of last year compared with an on-year drop of 2.1% in July. High street footfall fell 3.1% compared with a drop of 3.8% in July, while retail parks saw shopper numbers increase 1%, down from 1.2% in July. Shopping center footfall fell 0.5% in August compared with a 1.4% drop in July, according to the BRC. (ian.walker@wsj.com)
